title: Gating Example Setup
text:
Background
The original scripts per the README rely on CytoExploreR/commercial software to gate designated positive and negative populations, which then get exported out as .fcs files to designated folders.
To plug in to this existing workflow, we can modify the existing flowWorkspace, flowGate and Luciernaga steps from Signature Matrices to carry these steps out.


Set Up
Since this is my own contribution, the respective R packages would likely need to be installed.

if (!requireNamespace("flowWorkspace", quietly = TRUE)) BiocManager::install("flowWorkspace")
if (!requireNamespace("Luciernaga",
 quietly = TRUE)) remotes::install_github("https://github.com/DavidRach/Luciernaga")
if (!requireNamespace("flowGate",
 quietly = TRUE)) remotes::install_github("https://github.com/NKInstinct/flowGate")

Registered polygon_gate


Registered span_gate


Attach the R packages to your local environment

library(flowWorkspace)

As part of improvements to flowWorkspace, some behavior of
GatingSet objects has changed. For details, please read the section
titled "The cytoframe and cytoset classes" in the package vignette:

  vignette("flowWorkspace-Introduction", "flowWorkspace")

library(Luciernaga)
library(flowGate)

Loading required package: ggcyto


Loading required package: ggplot2


Loading required package: flowCore


Loading required package: ncdfFlow


Loading required package: BH

library(dplyr)


Attaching package: 'dplyr'


The following object is masked from 'package:ncdfFlow':

    filter


The following object is masked from 'package:flowCore':

    filter


The following objects are masked from 'package:stats':

    filter, lag


The following objects are masked from 'package:base':

    intersect, setdiff, setequal, union

library(stringr)

Identify the .fcs files, load into a GatingSet

UnmixingControlsFolder <- file.path("data", "unmixing_controls")
fcs_files <- list.files(UnmixingControlsFolder, pattern=".fcs", full.names=TRUE)
TheCytoset <- load_cytoset_from_fcs(fcs_files, truncate_max_range = FALSE, transformation=FALSE)
TheGatingSet <- GatingSet(TheCytoset)


TheGatingSet

A GatingSet with 6 samples


Don’t forget to transform with instrument appropiate settings

SFC_Parameters <- colnames(TheGatingSet)
FluorophoresOnly <- SFC_Parameters[!stringr::str_detect(SFC_Parameters, "FSC|SSC|Time")]

Biexponential <- flowjo_biexp_trans(channelRange=4096, maxValue=4194304,
  pos=5.62, neg=0, widthBasis=-1000)
MyBiexTransform <- transformerList(FluorophoresOnly, Biexponential)
transform(TheGatingSet, MyBiexTransform)

A GatingSet with 6 samples


Extract metadata, tidy until you have Fluorophore, Antigen and Type columns

pd <- pData(TheGatingSet)

Updated_cell_pd <- pd |> mutate(
    raw = str_extract(name, "(?<=PD_AD_)[^(]+(?=\\()"),
    Antigen = raw |>
      str_trim() |>
      str_extract("^\\S+"),
    Fluorophore = raw |>
      str_trim() |>
      str_remove("^\\S+\\s+") |>
      str_trim(),
    Type = name |>
      str_extract("(?<=\\()([^)]+)(?=\\))"),
    raw = NULL
  )

Updated_cell_pd <- Updated_cell_pd |> 
  mutate(Fluorophore = case_when(
    name == "Unstained (Cells)_scatter.fcs" ~ "CellUnstained",
    TRUE ~ Fluorophore
  ))

Updated_cell_pd <- Updated_cell_pd |>
    relocate(Fluorophore, Antigen, Type, .after="name")

Set up Gating Template

Template <- pData(TheGatingSet)
Template <- Template |> mutate(Detector="", Negative="CellUnstained")

Template <- Template |> mutate(
    Detector = purrr::map_chr(Fluorophore, \(f) DetectorGuess(x = f, NumberDetectors = 64))
  )

Create the initial gates. The borrowed example was downsampled and cleaned at the level of single lymphocytes so set to root, but would have been different here as needed.

# Run Manually
InitialUnmixSpanGates(template=Template, gs=TheGatingSet, subset="root", minpercentile=0.75, maxpercentile = 0.99)


# Run Manually
plot(TheGatingSet)


Check the gate placement via the flowGate shiny

# Run Manually
CheckUnmixingSpanGates(template=Template, gs=TheGatingSet, AdjustAll=TRUE)

We can then work on exporting the cells that are present within each gate out as their own .fcs file via the Downsampling.R file in the R folder.

TheDownsamplingFunction <- file.path("R", "Downsampling.R")
source(TheDownsamplingFunction)


NewNames <- Template |> 
  select(Antigen, Fluorophore) |> filter(!Fluorophore %in% "CellUnstained") |>
  mutate(NewName = paste(Antigen, Fluorophore, "pos", sep = "_"))


# purrr::map2(x=MyGatingSet, subset)



Take Away
At this point, the initial folders needed for this reproducible example have been setup, the minimal .fcs files for the example transferred in, and the neccesary packages present (or retroactively installed).

title: Reproducible Setup Example
text: This quarto document (.qmd) is intended to assist in the setup of a reproducible environement needed to run the .qmd files within this “Little Spectral Course”. This additionally permits the rendering of all the code chunks to produce Quarto Website pages, which in turn can be deployed to GitHub pages as a small Quarto website.

title: Reproducible Setup Example
Reproducible Setup Example
text:
Retrieving Dataset
This reproducible example can work with either your own .fcs files, or alternatively, we can retrieve the small downsampled dataset that is part of the Cytometry in R course (originally part of the TRU-OLS/AutoSpectral community walkthroughs).

RetrieveExternalDataset <- FALSE


if (RetrieveExternalDataset == TRUE){

    if (!requireNamespace("httr", quietly = TRUE)) install.packages("httr")
    if (!requireNamespace("jsonlite", quietly = TRUE)) install.packages("jsonlite")

    library(httr)
    library(jsonlite)

    owner  <- "UMGCCCFCSR"
    repo   <- "CytometryInR"
    branch <- "main"

    FullStainedSamplesPath <- "course/community/TRU-OLS/data/samples"
    UnmixingControlPath <- "course/community/TRU-OLS/data/unmixing_controls"

    #####################
    #      Samples      #
    #####################

    SamplesFolder <- file.path(DataFolder, "samples")
    if (!dir.exists(SamplesFolder)){dir.create(SamplesFolder)}

    api_url <- sprintf(
    "https://api.github.com/repos/%s/%s/contents/%s?ref=%s",
    owner, repo, FullStainedSamplesPath, branch
    )

    resp <- GET(api_url)
    stop_for_status(resp)

    files <- fromJSON(content(resp, as = "text", encoding = "UTF-8"))

    for (i in seq_len(nrow(files))) {
    if (files$type[i] == "file") {
        dest <- file.path(SamplesFolder, files$name[i])
        download.file(files$download_url[i], destfile = dest, mode = "wb", quiet = TRUE)
        message("Downloaded: ", files$name[i])
    }
    }

    #####################
    # Unmixing Controls #
    #####################

    UnmixingControlsFolder <- file.path(DataFolder, "unmixing_controls")
    if (!dir.exists(UnmixingControlsFolder)){dir.create(UnmixingControlsFolder)}

        api_url <- sprintf(
    "https://api.github.com/repos/%s/%s/contents/%s?ref=%s",
    owner, repo, UnmixingControlPath, branch
    )

    resp <- GET(api_url)
    stop_for_status(resp)

    files <- fromJSON(content(resp, as = "text", encoding = "UTF-8"))

    for (i in seq_len(nrow(files))) {
    if (files$type[i] == "file") {
        dest <- file.path(UnmixingControlsFolder, files$name[i])
        download.file(files$download_url[i], destfile = dest, mode = "wb", quiet = TRUE)
        message("Downloaded: ", files$name[i])
    }
    }
}


if (RetrieveExternalDataset == FALSE){
 
    #####################
    #      Samples      #
    #####################

    SamplesFolder <- file.path(DataFolder, "samples")
    if (!dir.exists(SamplesFolder)){dir.create(SamplesFolder)}

    message("Remember to transfer your full-stained samples to the 'data/samples' folder")

    #####################
    # Unmixing Controls #
    #####################

    UnmixingControlsFolder <- file.path(DataFolder, "unmixing_controls")
    if (!dir.exists(UnmixingControlsFolder)){dir.create(UnmixingControlsFolder)}

    message("Remember to transfer your unmixing controls to the 'data/samples' folder")

}

text:
Setting up GitHub Pages
If you want to share the website version on GitHub pages, there are a couple additional steps for setup after addition of the index.qmd and _quarto.yml files. First off, render the website via your terminal with the following

# In your terminal when at the working directory level, run 

quarto render

Once this is accomplished, add, commit and push your changes back to GitHub.
From there, navigate to Settings

Select Pages

Then select deploy from Branch, then the appropiate branch and docs folder.

At which point you should be set.
